Metronidazole, tetracycline, and bismuth subsalicylate are prescribed in specific dosages for 14 days, often in combination with an H2 antagonist, to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria. This approach aims to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria. 2. Tetracycline is contraindicated with acitretin due to the risk of increased intracranial pressure. 3. Dichlorphenamide increases bismuth subsalicylate levels through an unknown mechanism and is contraindicated. Co-administration with high-dose aspirin may elevate salicylate levels, leading to adverse effects such as anorexia, tachypnea, lethargy, and coma. 4. Metronidazole increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. It is contraindicated to use these drugs together. Metronidazole should be discontinued at least 14 days before starting dronabinol and should not be administered within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 5. Aluminum hydroxide reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. To avoid this, separate administration by at least 2 hours or use an alternative drug. 6. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and tetracycline can increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 7. Tetracycline increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Tetracycline reduces the effects of amoxicillin and ampicillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs, as tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used together. 9. Apalutamide decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. 10. Tetracycline increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may increase the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Metronidazole increases the levels of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib. 12. Tetracycline increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely and adjust the dose as necessary. 13. Tetracycline and metronidazole reduce the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 14. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Metronidazole increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Calcium salts (e.g., calcium acetate, carbonate, chloride, citrate, gluconate) reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 17. Carbamazepine decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Carbonyl iron reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Tetracycline and metronidazole reduce the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 20. Tetracycline increases the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may increase the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Metronidazole increases the levels of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 22. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Tetracycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Metronidazole increases the levels of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Disulfiram increases the toxicity of metronidazole by decreasing its metabolism, leading to enhanced central nervous system and cardiac toxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Metronidazole increases the levels of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Tetracycline increases the levels of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Tetracycline increases the levels of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Reduce the eliglustat dose in extensive metabolizers if co-administered. 30. Bismuth subsalicylate and eluxadoline increase each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of constipation-related adverse reactions. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Tetracycline increases the levels of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Enzalutamide decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Metronidazole increases the levels of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Metronidazole increases the levels of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Metronidazole increases the levels of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Tetracycline increases the levels of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 37. Ferric maltol reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Metronidazole increases the levels of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Ferrous salts (e.g., fumarate, gluconate, sulfate) reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Fexinidazole increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
